SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Continuous dry cough and runny nose for ~5–6 days; cough worse at night and disturbs sleep.
- Associated symptoms:
  • Chills/shivering at night; possible fever (temperature not measured).  
  • Generalized fatigue, myalgia (arms and legs).  
  • Brief diarrhea at illness onset, now resolved.  
  • No sputum production, chest pain, significant dyspnea, sore throat (only irritation from coughing), ear pain/discharge, nausea, vomiting, or urinary symptoms.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications:
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history:
  • Lives with partner.  
  • Occupation: IT developer (sedentary).  
  • Former smoker; quit 6 months ago.  
  • Alcohol: wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- No physical examination or vital signs documented.
- No investigations performed during visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute cough with coryzal symptoms  
   - Assessment: Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Bacterial bronchitis, early pneumonia, COVID-19, allergic rhinitis (less likely).  
   - Investigations: None at this time; consider review and chest assessment if symptoms persist >7–10 days or worsen.  
   - Treatment: Advise rest, adequate hydration, regular paracetamol for symptom control; take 1–2 days off work to recover; return sooner if breathlessness, persistent fever, or worsening cough. Possible antibiotics to be considered at follow-up if bacterial infection suspected.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus  
   - Assessment: Stable, self-monitored.  
   - Treatment: Continue Metformin; encourage adherence to diabetes follow-up appointments; reinforce general sick-day rules and monitor blood glucose during illness; limit alcohol intake as discussed.

3. Hypertension  
   - Assessment: Stable on Lisinopril.  
   - Treatment: Continue Lisinopril; alcohol reduction advice as above; routine BP monitoring to continue.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: No vital signs, chest/ENT physical exam, or medication dosages documented.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; no significant inaudible sections.
